ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Hasan delay the war with Syria despite having Jarīr as a hostage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hasan (peace be upon him) justifies his strategic delay of war with the Umayyads in Syria by using Jarīr ibn ‘Abdillāh as a political hostage, noting that his prolonged stay would inevitably lead to either deception or rebellion. This passage highlights the pragmatic balance between military readiness and diplomatic caution, reflecting the Shia scholarly view of the Imam’s calculated patience rather than mere weakness. The advice to 'plan and prepare' underscores the principle of *taqiyya* and strategic timing in the face of a powerful adversary.

en.sayed-ali-raza: My preparation for war with the people of Syria (ash-Sham)
while Jarīr ibn ‘Abdillāh al-Bajalī is still there would be closing the door for Syria and prevention of its people from good action (i.e. allegiance) if they intend doing it.
However, I have fixed a time limit for Jarīr after which he would not stay without either deception or in disobedience.
My opinion is in favour of patience, so wait a while. (In the meantime) I do not dislike your getting ready.
